You are a probe-script author on freytag-forge. Working directory: the real repository /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. Use .venv/bin/python with PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge and TMPDIR=/tmp; never use uv; run pytest with -n0. THIS TASK MAKES NO NETWORK OR BILLED CALLS and uses no credentials: do not source .env. No git add/commit/reset/clean/checkout/stash/push. You own ONLY scripts/ringer/stage7/quoted_name_probe.py, scripts/ringer/stage7/test_quoted_name_probe.py and files under bench/results/stage7-quoted-name-dry/. Do NOT edit narration_only_probe.py or segment_replay_probe.py; import capture_prompts, classify_body, _is_truncated, _make_provider, ANCHOR, RULE (or the equivalents; read both files first) from them, following how test_narration_only_probe.py imports.

QUESTION. With the narration-only rule in the system prompt, the 8B narrator still sometimes cuts its JSON off when a character names the program: it writes e.g. {"kind":"narration","text":"'It was called the "  with an unescaped double quotation mark around the program name inside the JSON string, so the reply is truncated and the spoken line is lost (truncated 10/20 control, 1/20 and 7/20 with the rule in two runs, 16/20 when the rule asked for single quotation marks). Test whether one extra system line stops the quoted name.

BUILD scripts/ringer/stage7/quoted_name_probe.py, run as `TMPDIR=/tmp PYTHONPATH=$PWD .venv/bin/python scripts/ringer/stage7/quoted_name_probe.py --n N --out DIR [--dry-run] [--confirm]`.
1. Use ONLY the 'dialogue' payload from capture_prompts (user string identical in every arm). Three arms, each inserting lines immediately BEFORE the anchor line 'Write each paragraph as one segment and return only JSON in this form:' (assert the anchor occurs exactly once): 'rule' inserts only this line:
Every paragraph uses the kind narration. Put spoken words inside the paragraph, in quotation marks. Do not use any other kind.
'no_name_quotes' inserts that line, then on the next line:
Write names and titles with no quotation marks.
'speech_only' inserts the rule line, then on the next line:
Use quotation marks only around spoken words.
Assert each arm's system with its inserted lines removed equals the original system and the user strings are byte-identical. Save the three payloads to DIR/arms/<arm>.json and write DIR/arms/system.diff (each arm diffed against an unmodified-system baseline, with the arm name in the header).
2. REPLAY (billed, only with --confirm): for rep in range(N), arm order rotates left by rep % 3, one POST per arm per rep built exactly like replay() in narration_only_probe.py (env vars read only inside the script, never printed, 60 s timeout). HARD CAP 60 worker calls, enforced before each call; refuse --n over 20; no retries; a row error is recorded and the run continues. Row fields: arm, rep, raw_body verbatim, error, truncated (reuse _is_truncated), plus classify_body fields (ok, invalid_kind, stray_selected_ids, bad_segments), kinds, and quoted_name = true when the raw inner narration text contains an escaped or unescaped double quotation mark immediately preceded by a space or by 'called' / 'named' / 'known as' within a segment text (keep this simple and document the rule in a comment; also count any double quote at all in the segment texts as double_quote_any). Write DIR/replies.jsonl and DIR/bad/<arm>-<rep>.txt for every non-ok or truncated row. DIR/summary.json: calls and per arm rows, ok, bad_rows, truncated, invalid_kind, quoted_name, double_quote_any, errors, mean_kept_chars (mean total characters of valid kept segments after the runtime's own repair, as narration_only_probe computes or can compute it).
3. --dry-run: prompt capture and arm build only, no network, summary calls 0. Without --confirm and without --dry-run refuse.
4. TESTS (no network): arm builder inserts exactly the intended lines in order and leaves user identical, fails on a missing or duplicated anchor; rotation gives each arm the first slot equally over 3 reps; cap stops at 60 with a fake sender; n over 20 refused; the quoted_name flag is true on a reply like `'It was called the "` style text and false on a clean reply.
HOW TO RUN AND VERIFY: pytest scripts/ringer/stage7 -n0, ruff check and ruff format --check on both files, then `TMPDIR=/tmp PYTHONPATH=$PWD .venv/bin/python scripts/ringer/stage7/quoted_name_probe.py --n 1 --dry-run --out bench/results/stage7-quoted-name-dry` and confirm DIR/arms/system.diff. Write DIR/notes.md (about 50 words). Do not run --confirm.
tasks.check: cd /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge && export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp && .venv/bin/python -m pytest scripts/ringer/stage7 -q -n0 > /tmp/qn.out 2>&1; tail -4 /tmp/qn.out; D=bench/results/stage7-quoted-name-dry/arms/system.diff; grep -q ' passed' /tmp/qn.out && ! grep -q ' failed\| error' /tmp/qn.out && grep -q 'Write names and titles with no quotation marks.' $D && grep -q 'Use quotation marks only around spoken words.' $D && test "$(grep -c '^-[^-]' $D)" = 0 && git diff --quiet scripts/ringer/stage7/narration_only_probe.py scripts/ringer/stage7/segment_replay_probe.py -- 2>/dev/null; .venv/bin/ruff check scripts/ringer/stage7/quoted_name_probe.py scripts/ringer/stage7/test_quoted_name_probe.py && .venv/bin/ruff format --check scripts/ringer/stage7/quoted_name_probe.py scripts/ringer/stage7/test_quoted_name_probe.py || { echo 'FAIL: see output above'; exit 1; }
